performers: Enrico Caruso, tenor; Salvatore Cottone, piano
intro: A husband in despair still has a show to give: Canio tells himself to put on his clown’s costume. Caruso sings the aria from Pagliacci with Salvatore Cottone at the piano, in Milan in 1902.

sections.label: A · Tenor and piano
sections.mNote: Caruso sings Canio; Cottone supplies the accompaniment

sections.label: B · The clown’s lament
sections.mNote: Canio’s grief inside a song about laughter

sections.label: C · The tenor’s last phrases
sections.mNote: Voice and piano carry the aria towards its close

sections.label: Coda · Closing bars
sections.mNote: The end of the piano-accompanied aria

cues.title: One piano, one tenor
cues.text: Salvatore Cottone supplies the whole accompaniment at the piano. There are only two musicians here: Caruso carries Canio’s part, and Cottone carries the theatre around him.
cues.evidence: The Discography of American Historical Recordings identifies Caruso, Cottone and the Milan session of 30 November 1902. https://adp.library.ucsb.edu/index.php/matrix/refer/1000003400

cues.title: The show must begin
cues.text: Canio has caught his wife Nedda with another man. Now Peppe tells him to get dressed: the audience is coming. Alone beside the little theatre, Canio has to turn his own humiliation into the clown’s act.
cues.evidence: Leoncavallo, Pagliacci (1892), Act I, final scene; libretto, Teatro Regio Torino, pp. 10–12. https://www.teatroregio.torino.it/sites/default/files/uploads/inline-files/20210807%20-%20Pagliacci%20-%20Libretto.pdf

cues.title: Laugh, clown
cues.text: The aria’s words are commands. Put on the costume. Powder the face. Turn sobs into a funny face. Canio orders himself to laugh at his broken love; the paying public expects a comedy.
cues.evidence: Leoncavallo’s Italian text for Canio in Pagliacci, Act I, “Vesti la giubba” through “Ridi, Pagliaccio”. The note describes the aria’s text as a whole. https://www.opera-arias.com/leoncavallo/pagliacci/vesti-la-giubba/
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.
